keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: Embodied vision-language-action models and world models
themes.summary: Papers advance embodied vision-language-action policies and world models for manipulation, navigation, driving, and flight, using pruning, routing, distillation, retrieval, benchmarks, and self-improvement. They differ in whether they adapt VLA policies for efficiency or memory, learn predictive world models in latent or video space, or contribute datasets and robustness evaluations.

themes.name: LLM benchmark evaluation and judge reliability
themes.summary: The papers introduce domain-specific benchmarks for LLMs and agents, spanning daily capability tracking, coding, operations research, games, spectral analysis, and other tasks, with attention to gaming, grounding, and real-time constraints. A second strand studies evaluation reliability itself, especially LLM-as-a-Judge bias, self-debiasing, rubric effects, label-free judge screening, and what aggregate benchmark scores conceal.

themes.name: Diffusion and flow-matching generative models
themes.summary: These papers apply diffusion and flow-matching generative models across autonomous driving, image and video editing, medical image synthesis, semantic communication, drug design, survival analysis, and human-object interaction. They differ in conditioning mechanisms such as quality ladders, classifier-free guidance, structural residuals, anatomy or tumor signals, and scene geometry, and in how they refine sampling through self-correction, tree search, reward fine-tuning, or test-time scaling. Other works extend the paradigm to discrete diffusion, diffusion language models, and concept erasure.

themes.name: Reinforcement learning for LLM agents and reasoning
themes.summary: These papers apply reinforcement learning to LLM agents solving multi-turn, long-horizon tasks such as web navigation, software engineering, tool use, programmable search, and medical reasoning. They differ mainly in how credit is assigned across a trajectory — from trajectory-level outcome rewards to step-level, counterfactual, or reparameterized credit — and in how training tasks, executable environments, and evolving skill libraries are synthesized and managed.

themes.name: Memory architectures for long-horizon LLM agents
themes.summary: The papers build persistent and external memory for long-horizon LLM agents across video, multimodal, conversational, and embodied settings, using structures such as event segmentation, parametric memory, revisable graphs, and Bayesian valuation. They differ in how memory is written, retrieved, governed, and allocated, and several contribute benchmarks or controlled comparisons of memory benefits and failure modes.

themes.name: Mechanistic interpretability and activation steering
themes.summary: These papers probe transformer internals, tracing how attention heads, latent representations, and sparse features encode and control behaviors such as concept recovery, prompt retention, language choice, safety, and planning. They differ in method and target: some use ablation, probing, decoding, or circuit analysis to localize internal signatures, while others develop activation-steering, gating, and SAE-based interventions for controllable or safer generation.

themes.name: Safety and robustness for LLM agents
themes.summary: The papers examine safety and robustness risks that arise when LLM agents read untrusted content, call tools, retain memories, collaborate, or act in physical and financial settings. They contribute attack methods and benchmarks for prompt injection, jailbreaking, agentic misalignment, privacy leakage, and loss of control, alongside defenses such as calibrated auditing ledgers, guard surface-form testing, and human-AI complementarity. Differences lie in threat model and evaluation target: multimodal intent splitting, multi-agent collusion, policy-dependent guardrails, and reasoning-trace monitorability.

themes.name: AI security, privacy, and provenance
themes.summary: The papers examine security, privacy, and provenance threats across generative media, biometrics, tabular models, and LLM agents, proposing detection and defense mechanisms such as adversarial training, robust evaluation, watermarking, dataset inference, and access control. They differ in threat model and target, ranging from physical spoofing and media forgery localization to prompt-injection, poisoning, preference-label attacks, and private function evaluation. Works also emphasize provenance and identity verification for agent-published data and dynamic agent systems.

themes.name: Time-series forecasting and spatio-temporal prediction
themes.summary: The papers develop forecasting methods across time-series, spatio-temporal, mobility, financial, weather, and process domains, mixing foundation models, attention mechanisms, decomposition, neural operators, and LLM-based evaluation. They differ in whether they target irregular temporal queries, spatial-temporal coupling, probabilistic multiscale horizons, volatility adaptation, physics-informed downscaling, or data-scarce event prediction. Several works emphasize reusable or parameter-shared forecasting operators, while others focus on leakage-aware evaluation and domain-specific covariates.

themes.name: Image restoration and computational imaging
themes.summary: The papers develop reconstruction and enhancement methods for varied imaging modalities, often combining learned priors, physics-informed models, and generative frameworks with measurement-specific conditioning. They differ in whether they target inverse-problem geometry, low-light or degraded imagery, spectral demosaicing, or data and degradation modelling for super-resolution and enhancement. Across these settings they emphasize robust priors, continuous or geometry-aware representations, and task-aware evaluation.

themes.name: Conformal prediction and calibrated uncertainty
themes.summary: Papers in this theme extend conformal prediction and calibrated uncertainty beyond simple marginal guarantees, addressing route-conditional coverage, fine-grained group and class disparities, multivariate prediction regions, dependence-aware certificates, and what conformal set size actually measures. Others use reliability and uncertainty signals for practical decisions such as abstention, early stopping, adaptive ensembling, and evidence-grounded extraction. The work differs in whether it contributes theory and audits, new conformal scores or calibration procedures, or plug-in reliability frameworks for deployed models.

themes.name: Clinical multimodal prediction and decision support
themes.summary: The papers build multimodal clinical prediction and decision-support systems that connect medical images, electronic health records, notes, and dialogue with interpretable or action-aware outputs. They differ in emphasis: some calibrate vision-language reasoning and decision thresholds, some model patient trajectories or treatment response, and others design evidence-grounded interaction and evaluation protocols for safe clinical use.

highlights.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2: A Cleaner, Harder-to-Game Coding Benchmark
highlights.authors: Soham Dan, Jeff Da, Sanyam Bhutani et al.
highlights.theme: LLM benchmark evaluation and judge reliability
highlights.why: A heavily revised, hardened SWE-Bench Pro split with 480 repaired or retired tasks and clean-container regrading, essential for trustworthy coding-agent evaluation.
highlights.key_result: SWE-Bench Pro V2 repaired or retired 480 of the 731 tasks and releases 642 tasks plus a 51-task Hard split; on the 642 V2 tasks frontier agents resolve up to 99.4% while other systems stay clearly separated, and the Hard split spreads systems from 52.9% to 98.0%.

highlights.title: What "Form'' of Uncertainty Does Conformal Prediction Quantify?
highlights.authors: Soroush H.Zargarbashi, Mohammad Sadegh Akhondzadeh, Rebekka Burkholz et al.
highlights.why: Clarifies that conformal prediction set-size differences quantify posterior variance or epistemic uncertainty and proposes formability as a useful uncertainty estimate.
highlights.key_result: We show that the difference in set size between full and split CP is directly connected to Bayesian posterior variance, which is the epistemic uncertainty of the model. It turns out that the model’s formability itself is a useful tool to quantify the epistemic uncertainty, and in our empirical evaluation it performs on par with the state of the art in many setups.
evidence: Conformal prediction (CP) is a post-hoc calibration method that returns prediction sets with distribution-free coverage guarantees, and the size of the output set is often interpreted as a notion of uncertainty. We show that the difference in set size between full and split CP is directly connected to Bayesian posterior variance, which is the epistemic uncertainty of the model. Essentially, this difference in set size is an aggregation of two opposite effects: (1) better model accuracy and therefore smaller set size achieved by training over extra calibration points, and (2) the ``formability'' of the model at test point towards every possible label. The latter effect vanishes with stronger models or more calibration data (as epistemic uncertainty is known for that behavior). It turns out that the model’s formability itself (without the quantization effect of prediction sets, and through estimating the posterior variance) is a useful tool to quantify the epistemic uncertainty. In our empirical evaluation it performs on par with the state of the art in many setups.

highlights.title: Do Conversational Agents Need Explicit Memory? A Controlled Comparison with Raw-History Retrieval
highlights.authors: Yongjie Zhou, Shuai Wang, Bevan Koopman et al.
highlights.theme: Memory architectures for long-horizon LLM agents
highlights.why: Controlled comparison finds explicit memory systems rarely beat raw-history RAG and pinpoints retrieval as the bottleneck, a useful negative result.
highlights.key_result: Across six state-of-the-art explicit memory systems compared with raw-history RAG on LongMemEval-S and BEAM-100K, the paper finds only localized gains for particular question types and tight run-time context budgets, with no consistent advantage over strong raw-history RAG baselines; oracle retrieval shows that some systems fail to preserve answer-supporting information during explicit memory construction, while others preserve it but fail to retrieve it effectively, despite construction costs reaching hours per conversation.

Oracle retrieval shows that some systems fail to preserve answer-supporting information during explicit memory construction, while others preserve it but fail to retrieve it effectively, despite construction costs reaching hours per conversation.

highlights.title: Who Gets Unmasked? Sampler-Induced Bias in Diffusion Language Models
highlights.authors: Xujun Che, Farsheed Haque, Depeng Xu et al.
highlights.why: Identifies a sampler-induced bias in diffusion language models that amplifies stereotypes and proposes fork-first sampling to mitigate it, with implications for fairness evaluation.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that the sampler changes who appears in generated text, a sampler-induced bias on top of the model's own. With the model and prompts fixed, LLaDA's default sampler writes a female manager in 21% of stories although the model itself puts 66% of its probability on a female protagonist; across 60 occupations the slope of its female share on the belief is 1.80, where exact sampling would give 1.

highlights.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
highlights.theme: Clinical multimodal prediction and decision support
highlights.why: Shows medical fine-tuning reshapes risk-bearing language independently of factual errors, motivating rubric-based safety evaluation for patient-facing LLMs.
highlights.key_result: First, ensemble risk-bearing language is statistically independent of factual hallucination rate (pooled Spearman = -0.065, n = 300, 95% CI [-0.18, +0.05]; distance correlation = 0.10, independence test p = 0.24), consistent with the two evaluation axes being statistically independent under this evaluation regime. Second, medical fine-tuning reshapes risk rather than reducing it: mean aggregate risk score differs by less than 0.2 across the six models with overlapping CIs, but continued-pretraining adaptations (BioMistral, OpenBioLLM) systematically suppress concrete actionable risk language while amplifying overconfident assertions (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.008 and p < 10^-4), whereas clinical instruction-tuning (Med42) suppresses dosing without amplifying overconfidence.

highlights.title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
highlights.theme: Safety and robustness for LLM agents
highlights.why: Shows LLM jailbreak graders can collapse the compliance class and proposes a free label-count check, with large implications for reported attack success rates.
highlights.key_result: Three dense graders of 8B and 9B parameters, from three model families, move compliant responses to the neighbouring class, evasion, instead of scattering them across classes. One of them assigns the compliance label zero times in 900 responses. On two corpora of 900 responses and eight graders, the compliance rate differs by a factor of 22 to 25, while the non-refusal rate differs by 18 to 23 percentage points.

highlights.title: Goal Images Are Control Targets: Spatially-Grounded Goal-Image Synthesis for Robotic Manipulation
highlights.authors: Riddhi Chatterjee, Ritish Shrirao, Kushagra Mehrotra et al.
highlights.theme: Embodied vision-language-action models and world models
highlights.why: Shows goal-image success depends on manipulation adherence rather than photorealism, overturning the use of generic image-editing metrics for goal-conditioned manipulation.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that image-editing quality is a misaligned proxy for goal-image utility: across two independent goal-conditioned policies on CALVIN, Gemini 3 Pro Image and GPT Image 1.5 produce worse control targets than the proposed finetuned open models, and SGE-Goal turns open base models into the strongest goal generators on CALVIN and second only to Gemini 3 Pro Image on SIMPLER-Bridge, sustaining roughly seven times the success rate at the longest (five-step) chains.
evidence: Across two independent goal-conditioned policies on CALVIN, the image editors that top aggregate editing-quality leaderboards (Gemini 3 Pro Image and GPT Image 1.5) produce worse control targets than our proposed far smaller finetuned open models, and the gap widens sharply for the multi-step (long-horizon) tasks robots actually face.
SGE-Goal turns open base models (FLUX.1 Kontext, FLUX.2 klein) into the strongest goal generators we evaluate on CALVIN, and second only to Gemini 3 Pro Image on SIMPLER-Bridge.
Base models fine-tuned with SGE-Goal also hold up under chaining far better than the best proprietary editor, sustaining roughly seven times the success rate at the longest (five-step) chains.

highlights.authors: Kazem Faghih, Yize Cheng, Shoumik Saha et al.
highlights.theme: LLM benchmark evaluation and judge reliability
highlights.why: Introduces accessibility profiles that reveal how breadth and reliability trade off beyond mean accuracy, changing how benchmark progress should be interpreted.
highlights.key_result: Across six benchmarks and more than twenty models, the paper shows that accessibility profiles reveal a tradeoff that accuracy hides: for about half of the model pairs with nearly equal mean accessibility, which model looks better depends on whether one success across five formulations is enough (Access@5) or all five must succeed (Reliable@5), and for some pairs the two measures diverge significantly, by up to 10 points in opposite directions.
evidence: Across six benchmarks and more than twenty models, this tradeoff is common: for about half of the model pairs with nearly equal mean accessibility, which model looks better depends on whether one success across five formulations is enough or all five must succeed, quantities we call Access@5 and Reliable@5, respectively. For some pairs the two measures diverge significantly, by up to 10 points in opposite directions.

For about half of the model pairs with nearly equal mean accessibility, which model looks better depends on whether one success across five formulations is enough or all five must succeed, and for some pairs the gap is significant, up to 10 points in each direction.

The largest case is LLaMA-3 8B versus LLaMA-3.1 8B on MMLU: with mean accessibility within 0.1 points, the former is 10.0 points higher in Reliable@5 ([6.3,13.8]) and 9.3 points lower in Access@5 ([-12.8,-5.8]).

news.title: Advancing coding in low‑resource programming languages
news.summary: OpenAI reported model advances for low-resource programming languages and introduced two evaluations: MultiLangBench, which tests building a SQLite-compatible database engine across 20 languages, and a COBOL migration evaluation. On MultiLangBench, GPT-6 Astra reached an average 87.4% test pass rate versus 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol, including COBOL rising from 10.9% to 72.1%; on COBOL migration, GPT-6.1 Sol reached 86.6% at low reasoning effort versus 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 97.9% at higher reasoning effort.

news.title: Germany Wants to Lead the World in Industrial AI: How NVIDIA Will Help
news.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang discussed Germany’s AI roadmap, focusing on industrial AI and manufacturing, at an event in Berlin. As part of the Invest in Germany Summit, the German federal government signed a Joint Declaration of Intent with NVIDIA to work on a joint initiative advancing cutting-edge AI models for physical AI and expanding collaboration with Germany’s Industry 4.0 Platform.

news.title: NVIDIA Advances Agentic Security for Media, From European Public Service Broadcasting to Global Content Production
news.summary: The European Broadcasting Union is collaborating with NVIDIA to expand its sovereign framework with sovereign cloud providers, open model developers, and systems integrators, including Microsoft Sovereign Cloud, Nebius, NVIDIA Nemotron open models, and Qvest. Adobe is using NVIDIA accelerated computing for Frame.io video search with NVDEC, TensorRT, and CUDA, reporting about 5x faster embedding generation, up to 4x higher throughput, up to 5x lower latency, and a two-frame-per-second proxy about 80% smaller than the 360p version it replaces.

news.title: Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile
news.summary: Jane Street implemented the Mamba-2 state-space model in NVIDIA CUDA Tile (cuTile) and partnered with NVIDIA to optimize three forward-pass kernels: chunk_cumsum, fwd_pass_state, and compute_out. The kernels use ct.cumsum for log-space decay cumulative sums, ct.mma for Tensor Core matrix multiplies, and a fused compute_out kernel with TF32 casting, plus optimizations including latency hints, operand swapping, transposed memory layouts, and an autotuner for block size and occupancy.

news.title: Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models on the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints, returning schema-compliant JSON via constrained decoding using JSON Schema output format and strict tool use. Compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours, and structured outputs work with batch inference and, on bedrock-runtime, cross-Region inference and streaming as typed events.

news.title: Developers can now access SageMaker Studio through the new AWS experience
news.summary: New Amazon SageMaker AI customers can sign up through the updated AWS experience using an existing Amazon, Apple, GitHub, Google, or email identity in 2–3 steps and land in a fully configured SageMaker Studio environment created in about 20 seconds. New customers receive $100 in AWS Free Tier credits, with a chance to earn an additional $100, and eligible accounts get default access to G5, G6, and G4dn GPU instances.

news.title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: 2026 year-to-date in review
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart reported onboarding over 100 new models from 30 distinct providers from January through September 2026, including 29 Alibaba Qwen models, 17 NVIDIA models, 7 Mistral models, 6 Google Gemma 4 variants, 4 IBM models, 4 Cohere models, and 33 from other providers. JumpStart covers model discovery and evaluation, one-click deployment, and customization techniques including LoRA, SFT, DPO, and RLVR.

news.title: Pegasus 1.5 from TwelveLabs is now available in Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: TwelveLabs’ Pegasus 1.5 is now available in Amazon Bedrock as a video language model that returns structured, timestamped JSON metadata for user-defined segments. It analyzes videos up to two hours long in a single request, up from one hour in Pegasus 1.2, and adds video segmentation, multimodal prompting with reference images, and on-the-fly processing from an Amazon S3 URI or base64 string without pre-indexing.

highlights.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2: A Cleaner, Harder-to-Game Coding Benchmark
highlights.authors: Soham Dan, Jeff Da, Sanyam Bhutani et al.
highlights.theme: LLM benchmark evaluation and judge reliability
highlights.why: 一个经过大幅修订、加固的 SWE-Bench Pro 划分，包含 480 个已修复或停用的任务以及干净容器重新评分，对于可信的编码智能体评估至关重要。
highlights.key_result: SWE-Bench Pro V2 修复或停用了 731 个任务中的 480 个，并发布了 642 个任务以及一个 51 个任务的 Hard 子集；在这 642 个 V2 任务上，前沿智能体最高可解决 99.4%，而其他系统保持明显差距，Hard 子集将各系统的表现从 52.9% 拉开到 98.0%。
evidence: Agentic audits, expert adjudication and blind re-implementation repaired or retired 480 of the 731 tasks: 23 contracted engineers spent 404 hours, each working in a language they write professionally, and every revised instruction was verified by a second engineer solving the task from the text alone.
On the 642 V2 tasks frontier agents resolve up to 99.4% while other systems stay clearly separated, and a 51-task Hard split spreads systems from 52.9% to 98.0%.

highlights.title: What "Form'' of Uncertainty Does Conformal Prediction Quantify?
highlights.authors: Soroush H.Zargarbashi, Mohammad Sadegh Akhondzadeh, Rebekka Burkholz et al.
highlights.why: 阐明共形预测的集合规模差异可以量化后验方差或认知不确定性，并提出将可成形性（formability）作为一种有用的不确定性估计。
highlights.key_result: 我们表明，全 CP 与分裂 CP 之间的集合规模差异直接与贝叶斯后验方差相关，后者即模型的认知不确定性。事实证明，模型本身的可成形性（formability）本身就是量化认知不确定性的有用工具，在我们的实证评估中，它在许多设置下与最先进方法表现相当。
evidence: Conformal prediction (CP) is a post-hoc calibration method that returns prediction sets with distribution-free coverage guarantees, and the size of the output set is often interpreted as a notion of uncertainty. We show that the difference in set size between full and split CP is directly connected to Bayesian posterior variance, which is the epistemic uncertainty of the model. Essentially, this difference in set size is an aggregation of two opposite effects: (1) better model accuracy and therefore smaller set size achieved by training over extra calibration points, and (2) the ``formability'' of the model at test point towards every possible label. The latter effect vanishes with stronger models or more calibration data (as epistemic uncertainty is known for that behavior). It turns out that the model’s formability itself (without the quantization effect of prediction sets, and through estimating the posterior variance) is a useful tool to quantify the epistemic uncertainty. In our empirical evaluation it performs on par with the state of the art in many setups.

highlights.title: Do Conversational Agents Need Explicit Memory? A Controlled Comparison with Raw-History Retrieval
highlights.authors: Yongjie Zhou, Shuai Wang, Bevan Koopman et al.
highlights.theme: Memory architectures for long-horizon LLM agents
highlights.why: 对照比较发现显式记忆系统很少优于原始历史 RAG，并指出检索是瓶颈，这是一个有用的负面结果。
highlights.key_result: 在 LongMemEval-S 和 BEAM-100K 上，将六种最先进的显式记忆系统与原始历史 RAG 进行比较，本文发现仅对特定问题类型和紧张的运行时上下文预算有局部收益，相对于强大的原始历史 RAG 基线没有一致优势；oracle 检索显示，一些系统在显式记忆构建期间未能保留支持答案的信息，而另一些系统虽然保留了这些信息但无法有效检索，尽管构建成本达到每次对话数小时。
evidence: This study compares six state-of-the-art explicit memory systems with raw-history RAG on LongMemEval-S and BEAM-100K under original and controlled retrieval settings.
We find only localized gains for particular question types and tight run-time context budgets, with no consistent advantage over strong raw-history RAG baselines.

Oracle retrieval shows that some systems fail to preserve answer-supporting information during explicit memory construction, while others preserve it but fail to retrieve it effectively, despite construction costs reaching hours per conversation.

highlights.title: Who Gets Unmasked? Sampler-Induced Bias in Diffusion Language Models
highlights.authors: Xujun Che, Farsheed Haque, Depeng Xu et al.
highlights.why: 识别出扩散语言模型中由采样器引发的偏差会放大刻板印象，并提出 fork-first 采样来缓解该问题，对公平性评估具有重要意义。
highlights.key_result: 本文表明，采样器会改变生成文本中出现的人物，这是一种在模型自身偏差之上的采样器引发偏差。在模型和提示固定的情况下，LLaDA 的默认采样器在 21% 的故事中写出女性经理，而模型本身将 66% 的概率分配给女性主角；在 60 种职业上，其女性占比对信念的斜率为 1.80，而精确采样应为 1。
evidence: We show that this second decision changes who appears in generated text, a sampler-induced bias on top of the model's own.

With the model and prompts fixed, LLaDA's default sampler writes a female manager in 21% of stories although the model itself puts 66% of its probability on a female protagonist (Figure a, b); across 60 occupations the slope of its female share on the belief is 1.80, where exact sampling would give 1 (Figure c).

highlights.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
highlights.theme: Clinical multimodal prediction and decision support
highlights.why: 表明医学微调独立于事实错误重塑风险承担语言，推动面向患者的 LLM 采用基于评分标准的安全评估。
highlights.key_result: 首先，集成风险承担语言与事实幻觉率在统计上独立（合并 Spearman = -0.065，n = 300，95% CI [-0.18, +0.05]；距离相关性 = 0.10，独立性检验 p = 0.24），与该评估机制下两个评估轴在统计上独立一致。其次，医学微调重塑了风险而非降低风险：六个模型的平均综合风险评分差异小于 0.2，置信区间重叠，但持续预训练型适应（BioMistral、OpenBioLLM）系统性地抑制具体可操作的风险语言，同时放大过度自信断言（配对 Wilcoxon p = 0.008 和 p < 10^-4），而临床指令微调（Med42）在抑制剂量相关风险语言的同时并未放大过度自信。
evidence: First, ensemble risk-bearing language is statistically independent of factual hallucination rate (pooled Spearman = -0.065, n = 300, 95% CI [-0.18, +0.05]; distance correlation = 0.10, independence test p = 0.24), consistent with the two evaluation axes being statistically independent under this evaluation regime.

Second, medical fine-tuning reshapes risk rather than reducing it: mean aggregate risk score differs by less than 0.2 across the six models with overlapping CIs, but continued-pretraining adaptations (BioMistral, OpenBioLLM) systematically suppress concrete actionable risk language while amplifying overconfident assertions (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.008 and p < 10^-4), whereas clinical instruction-tuning (Med42) suppresses dosing without amplifying overconfidence.

highlights.title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
highlights.theme: Safety and robustness for LLM agents
highlights.why: 表明 LLM 越狱评分器可能使合规类别坍缩，并提出一种零成本的标签计数检查，这对报告的攻击成功率有重大影响。
highlights.key_result: 来自三个模型系列的三个 8B 和 9B 参数的稠密评分器，将合规响应移动到相邻类别 evasion，而不是将它们分散到各个类别中。其中一个在 900 个响应中将合规标签分配了零次。在 900 个响应和八个评分器的两个语料库上，合规率相差 22 到 25 倍，而非拒绝率相差 18 到 23 个百分点。
evidence: Three dense graders of 8B and 9B parameters, from three model families, move compliant responses to the neighbouring class, evasion, instead of scattering them across classes. One of them assigns the compliance label zero times in 900 responses.
On two corpora of 900 responses and eight graders, the compliance rate differs by a factor of 22 to 25, while the non-refusal rate differs by 18 to 23 percentage points.

highlights.title: Goal Images Are Control Targets: Spatially-Grounded Goal-Image Synthesis for Robotic Manipulation
highlights.authors: Riddhi Chatterjee, Ritish Shrirao, Kushagra Mehrotra et al.
highlights.theme: Embodied vision-language-action models and world models
highlights.why: 表明目标图像的成功取决于对操作指令的遵循而非照片真实感，颠覆了在目标条件操作中使用通用图像编辑指标的做法。
highlights.key_result: 本文表明，图像编辑质量是目标图像效用的错误代理：在 CALVIN 上的两个独立目标条件策略中，Gemini 3 Pro Image 和 GPT Image 1.5 产生的控制目标比所提出的微调开放模型更差，而 SGE-Goal 将开放基础模型转变为 CALVIN 上最强的目标生成器，在 SIMPLER-Bridge 上仅次于 Gemini 3 Pro Image，在最长的（五步）链条上保持约七倍的成功率。
evidence: Across two independent goal-conditioned policies on CALVIN, the image editors that top aggregate editing-quality leaderboards (Gemini 3 Pro Image and GPT Image 1.5) produce worse control targets than our proposed far smaller finetuned open models, and the gap widens sharply for the multi-step (long-horizon) tasks robots actually face.
SGE-Goal turns open base models (FLUX.1 Kontext, FLUX.2 klein) into the strongest goal generators we evaluate on CALVIN, and second only to Gemini 3 Pro Image on SIMPLER-Bridge.
Base models fine-tuned with SGE-Goal also hold up under chaining far better than the best proprietary editor, sustaining roughly seven times the success rate at the longest (five-step) chains.

highlights.title: Revealing what benchmark scores hide: Jointly measuring the breadth and reliability of LLM capabilities using accessibility profiles
highlights.authors: Kazem Faghih, Yize Cheng, Shoumik Saha et al.
highlights.theme: LLM benchmark evaluation and judge reliability
highlights.why: 引入可及性配置文件，揭示在平均准确率之外的广度和可靠性之间的权衡，改变了基准进展应如何被解读。
highlights.key_result: 在六个基准和二十多个模型上，本文表明可及性配置文件揭示了准确率所隐藏的权衡：在平均可及性几乎相等的模型对中，约有一半情况下，哪个模型更好取决于五种表述中成功一种是否足够（Access@5）还是所有五种都必须成功（Reliable@5），并且对于某些模型对，这两种度量显著背离，在相反方向上相差最多 10 个百分点。
evidence: Across six benchmarks and more than twenty models, this tradeoff is common: for about half of the model pairs with nearly equal mean accessibility, which model looks better depends on whether one success across five formulations is enough or all five must succeed, quantities we call Access@5 and Reliable@5, respectively. For some pairs the two measures diverge significantly, by up to 10 points in opposite directions.

news.title: Advancing coding in low‑resource programming languages
news.summary: OpenAI 报告了低资源编程语言的模型进展，并引入两项评估：MultiLangBench，测试在 20 种语言中构建与 SQLite 兼容的数据库引擎；以及一项 COBOL 迁移评估。在 MultiLangBench 上，GPT-6 Astra 达到平均 87.4% 的测试通过率，而 GPT-5.6 Sol 为 26.8%，其中 COBOL 从 10.9% 上升到 72.1%；在 COBOL 迁移上，GPT-6.1 Sol 在低推理强度下达到 86.6%，对比 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 5.4%，在较高推理强度下达到 97.9%。

news.title: Germany Wants to Lead the World in Industrial AI: How NVIDIA Will Help

news.title: Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile
news.summary: Jane Street 在 NVIDIA CUDA Tile (cuTile) 中实现了 Mamba-2 状态空间模型，并与 NVIDIA 合作优化了三个前向传播内核：chunk_cumsum、fwd_pass_state 和 compute_out。这些内核使用 ct.cumsum 进行对数空间衰减累积求和，使用 ct.mma 进行 Tensor Core 矩阵乘法，并使用带 TF32 转换的融合 compute_out 内核，此外还包括延迟提示、操作数交换、转置内存布局以及针对块大小和占用率的自动调优器。

news.title: Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Amazon Bedrock 现在在 bedrock-runtime 和 bedrock-mantle 端点上为所有 Anthropic Claude 模型支持结构化输出，通过使用 JSON Schema 输出格式和严格工具使用的约束解码返回符合 schema 的 JSON。编译后的语法缓存 24 小时，结构化输出可与批量推理配合使用，并在 bedrock-runtime 上支持跨区域推理和作为类型化事件的流式传输。

news.title: Developers can now access SageMaker Studio through the new AWS experience
